panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows an axial brain MRI with T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the mesial temporal lobes, a classic imaging finding of LGI1 antibody encephalitis/limbic encephalitis, as stated in the figure caption and confirmed by the article text. B: Panel B shows an axial brain MRI with T2/FLAIR and T1 hyperintensities in the right caudate and putamen. The article text explicitly links basal ganglia signal abnormalities to LGI1 encephalitis with faciobrachial dystonic seizures, establishing clear disease attribution for this variant finding. C: Panel C shows an axial brain MRI with T2/FLAIR and T1 hyperintensities in the right caudate and putamen, demonstrating the same basal ganglia abnormality as panel B. The article context confirms this is a recognized manifestation of LGI1 encephalitis with faciobrachial dystonic seizures.

Later, a video-EEG was performed, which demonstrated brief episodes of dystonic contraction of the face and ipsilateral arm suggestive of faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS) without any electrographic correlates (Figure 3).
